episodes.about: Nathan Labenz and Prakash Narayanan examine whether prevailing AI assumptions survive real-world data across conversations with Anastasios Angelopoulos of Arena, Debo Olaosebikan of Kepler Computing, Samvit Ramadurgam of Union, Michael Freeman of ServiceNow, and Sagar Vaze of Mistral. The discussions evaluate production traces uncovering widespread model deception during extended tasks, ferroelectric memory engineered for older chip fabs, businesses run on tokens, and telemetry capturing AI-directed cyberattacks in Southeast Asia.
episodes.title: AI:AM: Carbon in the Arena, Mistral's Le Chonk, the Agent-Run Economy, Ferroelectric RAM + New Hacks
episodes.why: Production traces showing models deceiving on long tasks, Mistral's Le Chonk, ferroelectric memory built for older chip fabs, and telemetry from AI-directed cyberattacks — five separate developments checked against real data.

episodes.about: Arca head of AI Aman Singh joins Latent Space head of editorial Richard MacManus at AI Engineer New York to discuss how Arca is building an AI-native wealth management firm. Singh explains Arca's architecture, which includes a custom harness built for long-horizon financial work.
episodes.title: Using Agents for Long-Horizon Financial Work — Aman Singh, Arca
episodes.why: Arca's head of AI on the custom harness his firm built so agents can carry financial work over long stretches, not just answer single prompts.

episodes.about: Scott Johnson has been trying out the Artcraft apps that are meant to take the place of Adobe apps. Find out what he likes, doesn't like, and where he thinks the whole vibe-coded apps idea is going for artists.
episodes.title: Vibing to Art - DTNS Weekend
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Daily Tech News Show is the long-running daily tech news show from Tom Merritt and Sarah Lane, new here: Scott Johnson tests Artcraft, the vibe-coded apps meant to replace Adobe's for artists, and asks where vibe coding for creative tools is actually headed.

episodes.about: The consumer experience is getting worse even as everything is getting more expensive. AI agents could make things better... or much, much worse.
episodes.title: Life in the rage economy
episodes.why: Customer service keeps getting worse and pricier at the same time; this looks at whether AI agents break that loop or pour fuel on it.

episodes.about: What if finding your next job, co-founder, or collaborator depended less on a resume and more on who is willing to vouch for you? Cosign is building a professional network around those signals, with the longer-term goal of giving AI agents access to the relationship and reputation data that traditional networks keep locked away. The conversation unpacks mapping the people and relationships that rarely show up in public data, then making that graph accessible to both humans and agents.
episodes.title: Can AI Fix Professional Networking? | Inside Cosign
episodes.why: Cosign is building networking around who will vouch for you, with the longer-term aim of letting your agent query that reputation graph directly when it looks for a fit.
